## Reproduced source defect
Tested PR #170 head `8c6277ad59e5198b25672e3ec66587f04faca66e`, Node 24.22.1, isolated exact `src/params.ts`; no tracker writes or live integrations. This is not a published-package or full-release certification.

The documented boundary says values are trimmed strings and string parameters fully match their pattern. The accepted [pm-qz1k record](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-presets/blob/8c6277ad59e5198b25672e3ec66587f04faca66e/.agents/pm/features/pm-qz1k.toon) requires consistent parameter resolution across settings/templates/seeds with invalid inputs refused before writes.

## Minimal reproduction
```js
const manifest = [{
  name: "projectKey", type: "string", required: true,
  pattern: "[a-z]+", default: " acme "
}];
resolveParameterValues(manifest, {}).values.projectKey; // " acme "
resolveParameterValues(manifest, { projectKey: " acme " }).values.projectKey; // "acme"
```
Passing the first result to `resolveParameterizedPreset` with settings `id_prefix: "${param:projectKey}-"` produces `" acme -"`; a seed title bound to the same value becomes `" acme "`.

## Cause and impact
In [src/params.ts](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-presets/blob/8c6277ad59e5198b25672e3ec66587f04faca66e/src/params.ts), manifest validation checks `assertValueConstraints(parameter, assertPlainValue(...))`, but the default branch of `resolveParameterValues` assigns raw `parameter.default`. Caller-supplied values retain the normalized value instead. Thus an accepted default can emit characters outside its declared full-match pattern or exceed a maxLength validated only after trimming. Authoring the same logical value as a default versus an explicit input yields different native fields/prose and can trigger later native validation rather than the promised boundary.

## Expected / regression criteria
- Use one normalized effective-value path for defaults and supplied inputs (or explicitly reject noncanonical defaults consistently).
- Add default-versus-supplied parity regressions covering spaces/Unicode whitespace, full-match patterns and length boundaries, across settings/templates/seeds.
- Preserve input immutability and pre-write refusal behavior; keep secret-default refusal.
- Verify SDK and CLI consumers on the final head.

Seven bounded assertions confirmed the discrepancy, immutability, required/unknown-input refusals and secret-in-prose refusal. Full SDK/CLI/build suites were not run here; current PR gates were queued. The bundled default without surrounding whitespace is not claimed broken. All 170 all-status issue/PR records, current PR conversation/inline comments, and canonical item checked; no equivalent finding found.
